question: How do I find peace?
short_answer: The Quran places peace in remembrance, in trust, and in the nearness of Allah. It is not created. It is returned to.

sections.heading: Peace is in remembrance
sections.body: The Quran names remembrance as the place where the heart finds rest. It is a return, not a creation.

evidence.translation_en: Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts find peace.
evidence.why_cited: It names the place where peace is found.

evidence.translation_en: So remember Me; I will remember you.
evidence.why_cited: It shows remembrance is a two-way relationship.

evidence.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا
evidence.translation_en: O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.
evidence.why_cited: The command is for much remembrance.

sub_sections.heading: How is Dhikr different from Dua?
sub_sections.body: Dua is asking, while Dhikr is remembering. Dua is a moment. Dhikr is a state.

evidence.arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ
evidence.translation_en: And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near.
evidence.why_cited: It is about asking, which is Dua.

evidence.translation_en: Call upon Me; I will respond to you.
evidence.why_cited: It names the command to call.

sections.heading: Peace through trust
sections.body: The Quran places peace in trust. It is not passive. It is what you do after your effort ends.

evidence.arabic: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ
evidence.translation_en: And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him.
evidence.why_cited: It names sufficiency as the fruit of trust.

evidence.translation_en: And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah.
evidence.why_cited: It places trust after decision and effort.

evidence.translation_en: And upon Allah let the reliant rely.
evidence.why_cited: It names reliance as a practice.

sections.heading: Peace through nearness
sections.body: The Quran describes Allah as near. Not distant. Not delayed. Near.

evidence.arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ
evidence.translation_en: And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near.
evidence.why_cited: The 'say' is left out, and the answer comes directly.

evidence.arabic: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ
evidence.translation_en: And We are closer to him than his jugular vein.
evidence.why_cited: It describes closeness as physical and immediate.

evidence.translation_en: Indeed, my Lord is Near and Responsive.

sections.heading: Peace through the Quran
sections.body: The Quran describes itself as a healing and mercy. In its words, the heart finds what it needs.

evidence.arabic: وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَاءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
evidence.translation_en: And We send down of the Quran that which is healing and mercy for the believers.
evidence.why_cited: It names the Quran as healing and mercy.

evidence.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جَاءَتْكُم مَّوْعِظَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَشِفَاءٌ لِّمَا فِي الصُّدُورِ
evidence.translation_en: O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord and healing for what is in the chests.
evidence.why_cited: It names healing for what is in the chests.

evidence.translation_en: Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts find peace.
evidence.why_cited: It names remembrance as the place of peace.
